features.name: Hybrid BM25/FTS5 + Vector Search with Merge
features.description: SQLite FTS5 BM25 keyword results merged with vector embedding results via configurable vectorWeight/textWeight. buildFtsQuery joins all tokens with AND for precision. bm25RankToScore normalizes BM25 rank to [0,1].
features.counter_case: Requires SQLite FTS5 setup and optionally a vector backend (LanceDB); Cortex currently has no embedding infrastructure, making the vector half high-effort.

features.name: MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance) Diversity Re-ranking
features.description: Carbonell & Goldstein 1998 MMR algorithm via Jaccard similarity. CJK-aware tokenization (unigrams + adjacent bigrams). Token cache for efficiency. Lambda controls relevance vs diversity tradeoff (0.7 default). Normalizes scores to [0,1] before ranking.
features.counter_case: Adds O(n²) Jaccard computation after search; for very large result sets this could be slower than pure score sort.

features.name: Temporal Decay Scoring for Knowledge Age
features.description: Exponential half-life decay: score *= exp(-lambda * ageInDays). Extracts dates from file paths (YYYY-MM-DD.md). Distinguishes 'evergreen' files (MEMORY.md, undated memory topics) from dated entries. Falls back to mtime for non-dated files. Default halfLifeDays=30.
features.counter_case: Flaw #13 is about audit_quality uniform scores, but temporal decay here targets search ranking—not directly the audit_quality tool. Would still need to wire age-signal into audit_quality's formula separately.

features.name: Prompt-Cache Ordering Guideline
features.description: "Deterministic ordering for maps/sets/registries/plugin lists/files/network results before model/tool payloads. Preserve old transcript bytes when possible." Explicit rule in AGENTS.md to prevent prompt-cache invalidation from non-deterministic iteration order.
features.counter_case: Cortex's tool payloads are smaller and less frequent than OpenClaw's session-based calls; cache TTL impact may be lower.

features.name: Standing Orders Pattern (Permanent Operating Authority)
features.description: Template for granting agents permanent authority for defined programs: Scope + Triggers + Approval gates + Escalation rules + Execute-Verify-Report discipline. 'Do not batch unrelated issue fixes. Never retry indefinitely — 3 attempts max, then escalate.'
features.counter_case: Standing orders are a documentation/workflow pattern, not code; Cortex already has CLAUDE.md for agent guidance. Would mainly provide template structure rather than new capability.

features.name: Hook Lifecycle Event System (15 event types)
features.description: 15 typed events: command:new/reset/stop, session:compact:before/after, session:patch, agent:bootstrap, gateway:startup/shutdown/pre-restart, message:received/transcribed/preprocessed/sent. Hooks are directories with HOOK.md + handler.ts. Discovery precedence: bundled → plugin → managed → workspace. mutable event.messages[] to inject responses. W3C trace context in hook events for OTEL.
features.counter_case: OpenClaw's hooks run inside a persistent Gateway process; Cortex runs as a CLI/MCP server without the same lifecycle events. The 'gateway:shutdown' and 'session:compact' events have no direct Cortex equivalent yet.

features.name: Staggered Top-of-Hour Cron Scheduling
features.description: Top-of-hour cron expressions auto-stagger up to ±5 minutes to reduce load spikes. Explicit --exact flag to opt out, or --stagger 30s for custom window. Prevents synchronized ingest storms.
features.counter_case: Cortex is single-user local tool; load spike reduction is a non-issue at this scale. More relevant if Phase 22 (Central Knowledge Server) ships.

features.name: Prove-First / Ship-After-Review Gate (Bugfix Sweep)
features.description: Explicit two-phase gate: (1) Prove root cause + write regression test, produce dirty diff. (2) Human reviews, then one commit + changelog per accepted fix. Explicit skip criteria: not-a-bug, uncertain repro, guessed dependency behavior, no focused proof feasible.
features.counter_case: This is a workflow guideline for Cortex's own development process, not a user-facing feature. Could go in CLAUDE.md rather than shipping as a product phase.

features.name: Cron Multi-Session-Style Execution Model
features.description: Four execution styles: (1) main session — system event + heartbeat wake, (2) isolated — fresh transcript per run with browser cleanup, (3) current session — bound at creation, (4) custom session — persistent named context that builds on history. Each with different context carry semantics.
features.counter_case: Cortex's planned cron is simpler; the nuance between 'isolated' vs 'current' vs 'custom' only matters for multi-turn context-building. Cortex's agents are stateless today.

features.name: Heap Leak Detection via FinalizationRegistry + Heapsnapshot Delta
features.description: Structured leak triage: (1) reproduce failing shape, (2) wait for 2+ snapshot intervals, (3) classify via heapsnapshot-delta.mjs (module-graph growth vs real leak), (4) fix right layer (hotspot scheduling vs cleanup patch). FinalizationRegistry for tracked-instance counting. Three harness modes: closure-extracted (fix shape), closure-inline (pre-fix), synthetic-leak (harness validation). PASS/FAIL verdict on RSS delta.
features.counter_case: Cortex's MCP server is simpler than OpenClaw's gateway; heap leak surface is much smaller. The structured harness may be over-engineering for Cortex's current scale.

features.name: Evergreen vs Dated Memory Taxonomy
features.description: Files classified as 'evergreen' (MEMORY.md, undated topic files) are exempt from decay. Files named YYYY-MM-DD.md or datable by mtime decay at halfLifeDays=30. Prevents over-penalizing permanent reference knowledge while correctly aging ephemeral session summaries.
features.counter_case: Cortex's entities are code knowledge (not conversation memories), so 'freshness' semantics differ. Code never goes stale purely from age; it only goes stale when the source file changes.

features.name: Custom CodeQL Per-Boundary Security Scanning
features.description: 15+ scoped CodeQL configs, each targeting a specific trust boundary: auth-secrets, plugin-trust, network-SSRF, MCP-process, channel-runtime, config-boundary, etc. Only includes paths relevant to that boundary; excludes tests/fixtures/generated. Filters to security-severity 7.0+ at high/very-high precision. OpenGrep (Semgrep-compatible) handles changed-path scans in PRs.
features.counter_case: Cortex's codebase is 1% the size of OpenClaw; 15+ custom configs is overkill. One well-configured CodeQL scan + a Semgrep rule for path traversal would cover Cortex's actual attack surface.

features.name: Task Ledger (Background Work Activity Tracking)
features.description: Activity ledger for background work: queued→running→terminal states. Records: ACP runs, subagent spawns, cron executions, CLI operations. Push-driven completion (not polling). Notify policies: done_only, silent, state_changes. 7-day retention + auto-prune. CLI: tasks list/show/cancel/notify/audit/maintenance.
features.counter_case: Cortex doesn't yet spawn background agent processes; the task ledger is only needed once Phase 5.7 (Cron Engine) and Phase 53+ (Sub-Librarian Spawning) exist. Premature before those phases.

features.name: Process Lease + Reaper for Spawned Agent Processes
features.proposed_phase: Phase 53.4 refinement (Sub-Librarian Spawning with Context Inheritance)
features.description: Lease-based lifecycle management: each spawned ACP process gets a lease with sessionKey + rootPid + startedAt. Reaper cleans up OpenClaw-owned process trees via command-hash matching. Reset-aware session store marks sessions fresh on process reset. Prevents orphaned child processes across Gateway restarts.
features.counter_case: Cortex's sub-librarian spawning (Phase 53.4) is extended-vision; this pattern is only relevant post-Series-A. Installing dependency on `acpx/runtime` package would be a significant new dependency.

features.name: Memory Dreaming (Sleep-Cycle Memory Consolidation)
features.description: Three-phase cron-scheduled consolidation: (1) Light sleep — ingests recent daily memory files (4-line chunks, 280-char snippets, dedupe by similarity), (2) REM sleep — pattern detection with minPatternStrength threshold, (3) Deep dreaming — promotes short-term memories to long-term based on minRecallCount + minUniqueQueries + minScore + recencyHalfLife. Generates narrative summaries. Managed cron reconciliation with retry.
features.counter_case: Cortex's knowledge is code-synthesis, not conversation memory. 'Dreaming' over code entities is conceptually different; the scoring criteria (recall count, unique queries) only make sense for conversational systems.

features.name: CLAUDE.md as one-liner redirect to AGENTS.md
features.description: OpenClaw's CLAUDE.md contains only 'AGENTS.md' — a one-word redirect. All agent instructions live in AGENTS.md. This collapses two distinct instruction surfaces (IDE-specific Claude Code instructions vs general agent instructions) into one, losing the ability to have Claude Code-specific overrides.
features.why_target_chose_this: Simpler to maintain one authoritative file. Avoids duplication drift between CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.
features.proposed_action: Do NOT adopt in Cortex. Cortex's CLAUDE.md carries critical Cortex-specific rules (source MCP tool mandate, brevity stats) that differ from general agent guidance.

features.name: Break-glass dangerous flags without runtime warning injection
features.description: OpenClaw documents `dangerouslyDisableDeviceAuth` and `allowUnsafeExternalContent` flags but surfaces them only in static docs, not in runtime warnings when activated. Users enabling these flags get no in-process reminder that they've lowered security posture.
features.why_target_chose_this: Avoids noise in normal operation; trusts operators who deliberately set dangerous flags to read the docs.
features.proposed_action: Add to Cortex CLAUDE.md: any `dangerous*` config flag activation should emit a one-time startup warning visible to the operator.

features.name: On-demand vs cron-scheduled synthesis: which model fits Cortex?
features.question: OpenClaw schedules LLM consolidation at night (cron-based 'dreaming') to avoid interrupting work. Cortex triggers synthesis on every ingest. Should Cortex adopt a sleep-cycle model?
alternatives: (a) Keep on-demand synthesis — simpler, always fresh, fits 'ingest on commit' model
(b) Add optional cron-scheduled bulk consolidation for large repos — reduces per-commit LLM cost
(c) Both: on-demand for changed files, cron for idle-time quality passes across the full KB

features.name: In-memory fuse.js vs SQLite FTS5 for cortex_find
features.question: Flaw #18 calls for fuzzy matching. OpenClaw uses SQLite FTS5 (BM25, scalable, persistent). Cortex plans fuse.js (in-memory, simpler). Which is the right pick?
alternatives: (a) fuse.js — fast to ship, zero new deps, good for small KB (< 200 entities)
(b) SQLite FTS5 — scales to 10K+ files, BM25 ranking superior to Levenshtein, but adds SQLite dep
(c) Both phases: fuse.js now (Phase 0.9), SQLite FTS5 later (Phase 33.5 Unified Ingest Pipeline)

features.name: Should 'execute-verify-report' be a mandatory Cortex skill template requirement?
features.question: OpenClaw's standing orders mandate Execute-Verify-Report for every task. Should Cortex encode this as a required pattern in all skill SKILL.md templates?
alternatives: (a) Add to CLAUDE.md as a general agent discipline rule
(b) Add to each skill template's 'Output Expectations' section as a checklist
(c) Leave to individual skill authors — over-prescription reduces skill flexibility

features.name: Phase 13.5 RRF Ranker vs BM25
features.description: Cortex plans Reciprocal Rank Fusion (already shipped). OpenClaw uses BM25 from FTS5. BM25 is better for single-signal keyword ranking; RRF is better for fusing multiple ranked lists. For Cortex's use case (merging keyword + structural + path signals), RRF is more principled. OpenClaw's advantage: BM25 is already in SQLite, no extra implementation.
features.steel_man: BM25 provides more interpretable scores than RRF's 1/(k+rank) formula; simpler to explain to users why a result ranked higher.

features.name: Phase 2 LLM Synthesis Engine
features.description: Cortex synthesizes structured code knowledge (Role/Interface/Behavior/Wiring) from source. OpenClaw's memory stores conversational session summaries, not code entities. Cortex's synthesis approach is fundamentally different and purpose-built for code intelligence.
features.steel_man: OpenClaw's session-based approach is simpler and runs without AST parsing; Cortex's approach is more powerful but more fragile (hallucination risk on code structure).

features.name: Phase 4 MCP Server (Cortex IS the server)
features.description: Cortex exposes knowledge as an MCP server with 20+ tools. OpenClaw uses MCP as a client integration surface for external tools. Cortex's position as a server is stronger for IDE integration.
features.steel_man: OpenClaw's MCP client approach is more flexible — it can connect to any MCP server without being one, enabling richer multi-tool coordination.

features.description: MCP server integration — both projects use MCP
Secret sanitization — both have pre-commit secret scanning
Security CI gates — both use CodeQL and static analysis
CLI polish — both have rich CLI tooling
Git integration — both integrate with git for change detection
Hooks-based cache — both use hook events for bootstrap/cache invalidation
Knowledge storage — both use file-based knowledge stores

features.name: Multi-channel messaging (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal…)
features.description: Server-dependent. Requires persistent Gateway process and third-party API keys. 20+ channel extensions. Violates Cortex's local-first principle.

features.name: Mobile apps (iOS, Android, macOS)
features.description: Out of scope for a code knowledge tool. Cortex is developer tooling, not a consumer product.

features.name: ACP multi-agent orchestration framework
features.description: ACPX runtime requires persistent Gateway + external agent CLIs. Server-dependent. Extended vision (Phase 53+ in Cortex). Not appropriate until Cortex has paying customers.

features.name: ClawHub plugin marketplace
features.description: Server-dependent discovery platform. Cortex's local extension loading is sufficient for current scope.

features.name: Live model switching per-session
features.description: OpenClaw's agent can switch providers mid-run if primary fails. Cortex already plans Phase 0.14 (Multi-Backend LLM Abstraction); the per-session live-switch adds significant complexity without proportional code-analysis value.

features.name: Voice/audio transcription pipeline
features.description: Requires third-party TTS/STT APIs (ElevenLabs, Deepgram, Azure Speech). Out of scope for a code knowledge tool.

features.name: Deferred tool loading via meta-tools (TOOL_SEARCH_RAW_TOOL_NAME)
features.description: OpenClaw's tool catalog has 100+ tools; it uses meta-tools to search and load tool schemas on demand. For Cortex's ~25 MCP tools, this adds complexity without benefit. MCP already handles tool discovery natively.
